summary.headline: Small, low-return power producer with ten years left on its solar contracts; worth about Rs 2.80, not Rs 10
summary.text: LAUGFS Power PLC (LPL.N0000 voting, LPL.X0000 non-voting) sells all its power to the CEB from about 26 MW of solar plants (Hambantota and Embilipitiya) and mini hydro plants. Last year's Rs 461mn profit (EPS Rs 1.19) came from a Rs 544mn write-back of earlier impairments; without it the group made almost nothing. The six months to September 2026 were better (profit Rs 87mn, EPS Rs 0.23) thanks to the new 2 MW Pams hydro plant, but returns are still only about 4% of equity, the solar tax holiday has ended, the solar contracts run out in about ten years, and the parent, LAUGFS Holdings, owes the company Rs 521mn. No dividend is paid. At Rs 10.20 the share is 1.4x NAV of Rs 7.17. A whole-company DCF, P/E, price to book and a NAV check put fair value at about **Rs 2.83** (down from Rs 5.00, mainly because the brief's P/E and book-value methods are now applied to the low underlying returns). Buy at up to Rs 2.41; strong buy under Rs 2.13. The business fails three of four tests, so it stays in category 3 (avoid for now).

quality.reason: Low underlying returns, losses or near-losses in most of the last five years, and cash going to the parent rather than shareholders.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Reported 18.7% for 2025/26 came from the Rs 544mn reversal; without it about −3%. 11.9% in 2024/25 was lifted by Rs 376mn of one-off tariff billing; 2.7% in 2023/24. First-half 2026/27 profit of Rs 87mn is about 6% a year, but the second half is seasonally weak.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity
tests.note: Net debt Rs 1.55bn at 30 September 2026 against equity of Rs 2.78bn. About 4x the last 12 months' underlying EBITDA (Rs 0.39bn), above the usual 3x comfort level.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: 2024/25 relied on one-off billing and 2025/26 on the impairment reversal; the underlying 2025/26 result was a loss.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.value: No dividends; Rs 521mn lent to the parent
tests.note: Cash from operations was Rs 492mn in 2025/26 (Rs 253mn in the first half of 2026/27), but no dividend has been paid and LAUGFS Holdings owed the company Rs 521mn at March 2026.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods (whole-company DCF plus the money owed by the parent, P/E, justified price to book, NAV multiple) 30/50/20: Rs 1.48 / 2.96 / 4.57, giving Rs 2.83 (0.39x NAV). DCF, P/E and price to book come from scripts/valuation.py; discount rates from the beta (cost of equity 15.7%, WACC 13.5%). Down from Rs 5.00 on 11 November because P/E and price to book are now included, the DCF discounts at WACC with the end of the tax holiday, and lower maintenance-adjusted cash is assumed.

highlights.title: Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Revenue up 17% to Rs 480mn and profit up to Rs 87mn from Rs 23mn (EPS Rs 0.23 against Rs 0.06). Hydro revenue rose to Rs 91mn from Rs 22mn with the new Pams Power plant; solar was flat at Rs 389mn. Administrative costs fell 24%. The September quarter alone earned Rs 64mn (EPS Rs 0.17), the seasonal peak.

highlights.title: 2025/26: profit from a write-back
highlights.text: Profit Rs 461mn (EPS Rs 1.19) included a Rs 544mn reversal of earlier impairments (hydro Rs 291mn, solar Rs 253mn). Before it, operating profit was only Rs 31mn as generation fell 14% to 35.2 GWh and administrative costs rose to Rs 370mn. Revenue Rs 765mn against Rs 1,273mn, which had included Rs 376mn of one-off tariff billing.

highlights.title: Tax holiday over
highlights.text: The two solar companies' 10-year BOI tax exemption covered 2025/26 (effective tax 3%). From 2026/27 their profit is taxed at 30%: first-half tax was 20% of profit before tax.

highlights.title: Money with the parent
highlights.text: LAUGFS Holdings owed the company Rs 521mn at March 2026 (Rs 563mn a year earlier), more than the CEB's Rs 204mn of trade receivables. Total receivables rose to Rs 1.07bn by September; the interim doesn't split them.

highlights.title: Growth plans cut back
highlights.text: The 2 MW Pams hydro plant was finished, but the report's own plan table marks the 10 MW Hambantota solar expansion and the 50 MW Mannar wind project as cancelled (only Phase 1, 1.4 MW DC, was added). No capital commitments at March 2026.

methodReadings.reading: The price is 1.42x NAV. Book value rests on plants with about ten years of solar contracts left; the company's own valuation (15.3–16.3% discount rates) supports roughly book.
Far below the 15.7% cost of equity, so each rupee of book earns too little to be worth a rupee.
Next year's EPS Rs 0.18 / 0.28 / 0.38 at a justified P/E of about 6.
No dividend for 2025/26 or so far this year, so a dividend model can't be used.
Cash before interest of Rs 0.20–0.43bn a year to about 2036, then shrinking, at WACC, less Rs 1.55bn net debt, plus the money owed by the parent.

models.name: Whole-company DCF (WACC, less net debt) + money owed by the parent
models.comment: Cash before interest after tax and maintenance capex of Rs 0.20 / 0.33 / 0.43bn (EBITDA about Rs 450 / 520 / 600mn, less tax at 30% on operating profit, less maintenance Rs 200 / 120 / 80mn), after-tax operating profit Rs 0.11 / 0.16 / 0.22bn, changing −1% / 0% / 1% a year for ten years while the solar contracts run, then −5% / −3% / +1% a year (lower tariffs after the contracts, ageing plants; the bull assumes contracts renewed or the plants repowered), at a 12% return on new capital, discounted at WACC 14.6% / 13.5% / 12.5% (scripts/reinvestment.py). Firm value Rs 1.30 / 2.37 / 3.62bn; 21–34% of it comes after year 10. Less net debt Rs 1.55bn (30 September 2026): Rs −0.66 / 2.12 / 5.34 a share. Plus Rs 0.521bn owed by LAUGFS Holdings at 50% / 80% / 100% (Rs 0.67 / 1.08 / 1.35). The shrinking long run in the bear and base frees a little capital in the formula (growth ÷ return on capital), which slightly flatters them.

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: EPS for the year to March 2027 of Rs 0.18 / 0.28 / 0.38 times a justified forward P/E of 5.8 / 6.4 / 6.3 at the cost of equity (17.2 / 15.7 / 14.2%), with ROE 3 / 4 / 6% and long-run growth 0 / 0 / 1%. First-half EPS was Rs 0.23; the second half is the weak season (2025/26's second half lost money before the reversal) and now carries 30% tax. The base is 76% below the Rs 1.19 'run-rate', which is the reversal year; the Rs 0.68 'latest quarter × 4' is the monsoon peak quarter.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: Book value Rs 7.17 (30 September 2026) × (ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 3 / 4 / 6%, growth 0 / 0 / 1%, cost of equity 17.2 / 15.7 / 14.2%. An ROE far below the 15.7% cost of equity is outside the normal range, and right here: the plants earn fixed tariffs with high depreciation and finance costs.

models.name: NAV multiple
models.comment: 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 times NAV of Rs 7.17. Book value is close to the company's own DCF of its plants (Rs 6.51 a share at parent level, using 15.3–16.3% discount rates), but the plants are wasting assets earning about 4% on equity.

modelsNote: A small contracted power producer suits a whole-company DCF over the remaining contract life (ten growth years instead of five, because the solar contracts run about ten more years), plus the Rs 0.52bn owed by the parent. P/E and justified price to book use the cost of equity and show how little the low underlying ROE is worth; NAV is a cross-check. No dividend is paid, so there is no dividend model. Growth check: assumed −1% / 0% / 1% against −5.2% supported (reinvestment rate −757% × return on capital 0.7%, FY2026); the supported figure comes from a year with only Rs 31mn underlying operating profit and Rs 187mn of receivables collected, so it isn't a fair guide; fixed tariffs, a full year of the new Pams hydro plant and Phase 2 at Hambantota justify flat output, with the bull's 1% needing Phase 2 to be built.

scenarios.common: Net debt Rs 1.55bn and NAV Rs 7.17 at 30 September 2026. 387.0 million shares (335.0mn voting, 52.0mn non-voting), valued the same. Price Rs 10.20 (CSE close 19 Nov 2026). Solar contracts have about ten years left (note 7.1.6); the Pams hydro contract runs 20 years. Solar profit is taxed at 30% from 2026/27.

sensitivity.title: Whole-company DCF + parent receivable, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Base-case growth (0% then −3%), parent receivable at 80%. Rs 10.20 would need cash of about Rs 0.8bn a year, roughly double the best year, or contracts extended well beyond their terms.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 1,250 in total, against Rs 5,100 at Rs 10.20.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 2.41 needs a fall of about 76%. The voting share hasn't traded below Rs 10.00 since 2024/25 (its low in that year was Rs 8.40, in April 2024), so the buy price isn't realistic soon. The non-voting share (Rs 8.30) has the same claim on profits and is 19% cheaper, but still far above the buy price.

higher: The parent repaying the Rs 521mn it owes, or paying it out as a dividend.
Solar contracts extended at good tariffs, or the plants repowered on new contracts.
Phase 2 of the Hambantota expansion built and earning well.
Underlying ROE rising towards 10% with the new hydro plant.
lower: More money lent to LAUGFS group companies.
Lower output or tariff cuts by the CEB, or slower CEB payments.
Another impairment as the contracts near their end.
Higher interest rates on its floating-rate loans (AWPLR + 1–2%).

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2025/26 annual report and the interim report to 30 September 2026 (a scanned document read from its page images, so check any figure that matters), with earlier years from the five-year summary. The price is the CSE close of 19 November 2026. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
Summary: LAUGFS Power PLC (LPL.N0000 voting, LPL.X0000 non-voting) sells all its power to the CEB from about 26 MW of solar (Hambantota, Embilipitiya) and mini hydro plants. Last year's Rs 461mn profit (EPS Rs 1.19) came from a Rs 544mn write-back of earlier impairments; without it the group made almost nothing. The first half of 2026/27 was better (profit Rs 87mn, EPS Rs 0.23) thanks to the new 2 MW Pams hydro plant, but underlying return on equity is only about 4%, the solar tax holiday has ended, the solar contracts end in about ten years and the parent owes the company Rs 521mn. No dividend. At Rs 10.20 the share is 1.4x NAV of Rs 7.17. Fair value about Rs 2.83 (was Rs 5.00): buy at up to Rs 2.41, strong buy under Rs 2.13. Business tests: 1 of 4, category 3 (avoid for now), unchanged.

Price and key figures
Price Rs 10.20 voting, Rs 8.30 non-voting (CSE close, 19 November 2026). Market cap about Rs 3.85bn; net debt Rs 1.55bn; EV about Rs 5.40bn, 13.8x last-12-months underlying EBITDA of Rs 0.39bn.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 480mn (up 17%), operating profit Rs 184mn (Rs 99mn), profit Rs 87mn (Rs 23mn), EPS Rs 0.23 (Rs 0.06). Hydro revenue Rs 91mn (Rs 22mn), solar Rs 389mn (Rs 387mn). Cash from operations Rs 253mn; capex Rs 67mn.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 765mn, generation 35.2 GWh (down 14%), operating profit Rs 31mn before the Rs 544mn reversal, profit Rs 461mn, EPS Rs 1.19. Effective tax 3% (BOI holiday); 30% from now on.
NAV Rs 7.17 a share. LAUGFS Holdings owns 74.0% of the voting shares and owed the company Rs 521mn at March.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Whole-company DCF + parent receivable | 0.01 | 3.20 | 6.69 | 2.94
P/E | 1.05 | 1.78 | 2.40 | 1.69
Justified price to book | 1.25 | 1.83 | 2.72 | 1.83
NAV multiple | 3.59 | 5.02 | 6.45 | 4.88
Average | 1.48 | 2.96 | 4.57 | 2.83
Fair value Rs 2.83 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 2.41 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 2.13 (25% below).

Required return
Beta 0.73 (renewable-energy sector beta relevered for LPL's debt; no local betas). Cost of equity 15.7% (bear 17.2%, bull 14.2%); cost of debt 8.3%; WACC 13.5% (14.6% / 12.5%).

Assumptions
DCF: EBITDA Rs 450 / 520 / 600mn a year, less 30% tax on operating profit and maintenance capex of Rs 200 / 120 / 80mn, gives cash of Rs 0.20 / 0.33 / 0.43bn; −1% / 0% / +1% a year for the ten contract years, then −5% / −3% / +1%. Maintenance is below depreciation (Rs 261mn) because solar panels aren't replaced during the contracts and repairs (Rs 62mn) are already expensed; that's outside the usual 0.8–1.3x range and is explained here. The parent's Rs 521mn debt counts at 50% / 80% / 100%.
P/E: EPS Rs 0.18 / 0.28 / 0.38 for 2026/27 at justified P/Es of about 6. Price to book: ROE 3 / 4 / 6%. NAV: 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9x.
Growth check: the calculator's supported growth is −5.2% from 2025/26, a year with almost no operating profit and a working-capital release; flat output on fixed tariffs is assumed instead.
Earnings check: the base EPS is far below the 'run-rate' because that is the reversal year (Rs 1.19) or the monsoon-peak quarter × 4 (Rs 0.68).

What stands out
- Last year's profit was an accounting write-back; underlying returns are about 4%.
- The parent owes the company Rs 521mn, more than the CEB does; nothing comes back as dividends.
- The tax holiday has ended, so profit after tax will be lower for the same output.
- The plan table cancels the 10 MW Hambantota expansion and the 50 MW Mannar wind project.
- Debt is moderate against equity (0.56x) but about 4x EBITDA.

Management and plans
Management promises better output from existing plants, Phase 2 at Hambantota, storage studies, a possible merger of other LAUGFS renewable companies and a move into MEP contracting. Delivered: the Pams hydro plant. Missed: the 10 MW Hambantota expansion and the Mannar wind project; finance costs rose 16% in the first half.

Shareholders
LAUGFS Holdings 74.0% of voting shares; EPF 12.3%. Almas Holdings sold about 0.6m voting and 0.9m non-voting shares in the half. 8,706 public holders.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 2.83, 150 up to Rs 2.41, 150 up to Rs 2.13: average about Rs 2.49, about Rs 1,250 in total. Rs 2.41 needs a 76% fall; the voting share's lowest price since April 2024 is Rs 10.00.

What would change my view
Higher: the parent repaying or paying out its debt, contracts extended or plants repowered, Phase 2 earning well, ROE towards 10%.
Lower: more lending to the group, lower output or tariffs, another impairment, higher loan rates.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt): avoid for now (category 3, unchanged).

dcf.addOnNote: Rs 0.521bn owed by the parent, LAUGFS Holdings (31 March 2026), counted at 50% / 80% / 100%: Rs 0.67 / 1.08 / 1.35 a share

requiredReturn.betaBasis: Provisional. Damodaran's global Green & Renewable Energy unlevered beta 0.57 (January 2026; stand-in, as his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened), relevered at net debt 0.40x market value (Rs 10.20 voting, Rs 8.30 non-voting) with 30% tax: 0.73. No local 5-year betas found. Refresh in January 2027.
sources: Default spread 4.0%: market-based, Sri Lanka dollar bonds vs US Treasuries (14 Nov 2026)
Mature-market premium 4.2% and volatility factor 1.52: Damodaran, Country Risk, July 2026
Cost of debt: interest paid Rs 0.147bn ÷ average borrowings and leases Rs 1.77bn (Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 109, 134, 140)
Weights: Rs 3.95bn equity (387mn shares at Rs 10.20, CSE close 19 Nov 2026), net debt Rs 1.55bn (30 Sep 2026)
requiredReturn.note: Cost of equity = 8.24% + 0.73 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 15.7%; bear +1.5, bull −1.5 points. Inside the 12–22% range. WACC weights equity 71.8% and debt 28.2% at 8.31% less 3.3% tax (2025/26's effective rate, inside the tax holiday; at 30% tax WACC would be about 0.6 points lower). The calculator values both share classes at the voting price.

management.source: Annual Report 2025/26: Group Chairman (pp. 10–11), Group Executive Vice Chairman (pp. 12–13), acting Group MD (pp. 14–15), MD/CEO (pp. 16–18), Review of Operations (p. 43), Manufactured Capital (p. 47), Future Direction (p. 51), notes 7, 12 and 19; progress from Interim to 30 Sep 2026
management.takeaway: Management talks of growth in solar, wind and storage, but its own plan table cancels the two big projects; for now the story is squeezing more from small existing plants, while cash sits with the parent rather than reaching shareholders.

said.text: Profit of Rs 461mn was helped by a Rs 544mn impairment reversal; the company itself made a loss of Rs 129mn
Generation fell about 15% on weather; finance costs fell 24% to Rs 158mn
Debt service cover improved to 1.8 times from 1.4; return on capital employed 14.6%
The sector faces curtailment, grid limits, slow approvals and changing tariffs
Operating fixes have already lifted output at the Iris and Anorchi solar plants

Phase 2 of the Hambantota solar expansion under way (Phase 1 added 1.4 MW DC)
Study battery storage and solar-hydro hybrids; pilots in the medium term
Possibly merge other LAUGFS renewable companies into LAUGFS Power
Expand into mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) contracting

track.promise: Reverse losses into profits and improve cash generation

First-half finance cost Rs 99mn, up 16% from Rs 85mn
